column1: # BATCH 18 — pitch layout most=E high=G mid=G low=E least=G
# Elevated slots are MOST and LOW. MOST TAKES LANE A — most is the excess in all five,
# which is an overshoot with a consequence, and irreversibility suits it exactly. LOW
# TAKES LANE B — low is a withdrawal or a single concession, and jeopardy deflates
# those; access does not.
# The axis work below is done against the three source files for each entry and against
# every neighbouring trait already written. THE POLES ARE FIXED. Steps 2-8 are worked on
# top of this; do not re-derive the axes, and do not quietly widen a pole to fit a scene
# you like. If a scenario will not sit on the pole as written, the scenario is wrong.
# Rows are still to be added at step 4. Run `plan` before any prose exists.
# === umami-roasted-fava — defiant / insubordinate / submissive
# AXIS: something with actual power over you has told you to stop, and named or implied
#   what it can do about it, and you go on anyway where it can be seen. Fava moves toward
#   the difficult thing and starts before the outcome is safe; roasted develops OUTWARD,
#   in front of everyone, so nothing here is quiet or sly; umami is the slow one, so this
#   is a refusal kept up over time rather than one hot moment.
# NOT: headstrong (spicy-fried-green, approved). Headstrong is the reader's own will
#   against ADVICE — parents, a boss offering a raise, everyone saying pull out. Nobody in
#   those five can DO anything to the reader; they can only be wrong at them. Defiant needs
#   A POWER THAT CAN ACTUALLY IMPOSE SOMETHING, AND THE SANCTION HAS TO BE ON THE PAGE —
#   the ban, the fine, the removal, the losing of the thing. If the only consequence of the
#   act is that people disapprove, it is headstrong and it is wrong.
#   NOT firm (sour-dried-navy, batch 05 — a position that does not move when pushed; there
#   is no authority in it). NOT irreverent (sour-roasted-pinto, batch 03 — treating the
#   grand thing lightly; defiance is not a joke and takes the power seriously enough to
#   break with it). NOT subversive (spicy-fermented-fava, queued — SAME BEAN, and it works
#   underneath; roasted means this is done in the open, which is the separation to keep).
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  insubordinate — the refusal has stopped being about the thing it started over.
#         You go on breaking with them where it costs somebody who is not you, and you
#         will not be reached on any terms they can offer.
#   HIGH  defiant — the sanction is stated and real, and you do the forbidden thing openly,
#         under your own name, and pay for it.
#   MID   defiant, low pitch — a standing instruction from someone with genuine power over
#         you, visibly not complied with, in something small enough that only you carry it.
#   LOW   submissive, low pitch — you comply once against your own view, and the reason is
#         stated. Not agreeableness: it must be an instruction obeyed.
#   LEAST submissive — you do exactly as told, openly and fully, and you are settled about
#         it rather than sour. WATCH: not being nice, not being a team player. It is the
#         instruction being taken as an instruction and that being fine.
# === umami-dried-adzuki — reverential / awestruck / profane
# AXIS: something greater than you is present and you conduct yourself the way it asks,
#   at cost, whether or not anybody is checking. Adzuki knows which moments deserve to be
#   marked and marks them fully; dried undergoes nothing and keeps a thing intact for as
#   long as keeping takes; umami is depth and slowness, so the observance is a settled
#   practice rather than a mood.
# NOT: solemn (umami-smoked-black, batch 15). Solemn treats a thing as WEIGHING WHAT IT
#   WEIGHS, on its own terms, with nothing above the reader — the last press going off,
#   the logbook since 1928. Reverential POINTS UP: THERE HAS TO BE SOMETHING GREATER THAN
#   THE READER ON THE PAGE, and the reader is the smaller party. If the reader is simply
#   giving a thing its proper weight, it is solemn and it is wrong.
#   NOT antiquarian (bitter-fermented-adzuki, batch 03 — SAME BEAN). Antiquarian is the
#   OLD OBJECT AND ITS KEEPING — account books, the county archive, the boxes in the loft.
#   What is revered here NEED NOT BE OLD AT ALL, and no facet may turn on age or on an
#   artefact being preserved.
#   NOT hallowed (umami-smoked-adzuki, queued) and NOT ceremonious (bitter-boiled-adzuki,
#   queued — the FORM observed for its own sake). Nothing supernatural is required and no
#   facet needs a religion.
# NOTE ON THE INVERSE: profane means HANDLING THE SACRED THING AS ORDINARY MATERIAL — the
#   good plates used for beans on toast. It does not mean swearing, and it does not mean
#   being disrespectful to a person.
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  awestruck — the greatness takes you out of service. In front of it you cannot do
#         the plain thing somebody was relying on you to do, and they carry that.
#   HIGH  reverential — a real and stated cost paid to keep the form the thing asks for,
#         when the shortcut was available and nobody would have known.
#   MID   reverential, low pitch — a small observance kept while everyone around you is
#         handling the same thing casually, at a cost only to you.
#   LOW   profane, low pitch — you put it to ordinary use once, deliberately, for a stated
#         practical reason.
#   LEAST profane — the thing is treated as plain material, in the open, and you are
#         settled about it. The price of that is visible; it is a position, not a lapse.
# === sour-smoked-mung — revealing / exposing / concealing
# AXIS: something is being kept out of sight, for a reason the page states, and you bring
#   it into view. Mung is the healer, so at the trait poles the bringing-out is FOR THE
#   GOOD OF WHAT IS REVEALED; smoked works with no visible cause, so the reader's hand in
#   it is never announced; sour cuts the thing down to what is actually true.
# NOT: confiding (umami-roasted-cannellini, approved). Confiding is telling somebody
#   something private ABOUT YOURSELF, to them, as trust — the tattooist, the hospital
#   chair, the washing-up. REVEALING IS MAKING SOMETHING VISIBLE THAT WAS BEING KEPT OUT
#   OF SIGHT, AND IT NEED NOT BE THE READER'S OWN — which is exactly why the excess is
#   exposing rather than oversharing. If a facet works by the reader disclosing their own
#   business, it is confiding and it is wrong.
#   NOT frank / forthright / blunt (sour-roasted-cannellini b01, sour-roasted-edamame b02,
#   sour-fried-edamame b16) — those are all MANNER OF SPEECH, saying the hard thing
#   straight. Revealing is about a thing coming into view, and the reader may say very
#   little. NOT piercing (sour-smoked-cannellini, batch 09 — SAME FLAVOUR AND SAME FORM;
#   that is seeing through somebody, an act of perception. This is an act of disclosure,
#   and what is uncovered is already known to somebody).
# DESIGN RULE: EVERY FACET STATES WHY THE THING WAS BEING KEPT BACK. Without the reason
#   there is nothing being uncovered, only a fact mentioned, and Accept collapses into
#   "yes, I talk about things".
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  exposing — you put it in front of people who cannot un-see it, and the person
#         whose thing it was had a reason and did not choose the moment. It serves the
#         truth and not them.
#   HIGH  revealing — real cost to you, and what was being hidden gets seen by the person
#         who needed to see it, for the good of the one who was hiding it.
#   MID   revealing, low pitch — a small covered thing brought into the open where leaving
#         it covered would have been easy and unnoticed, at a cost only to you.
#   LOW   concealing, low pitch — you keep one thing out of sight once, for a stated reason.
#   LEAST concealing — you actively keep the cover on, openly, and you hold that hidden is
#         the better state. Settled, not cowardly.
# === spicy-fried-black — relentless / remorseless / relenting
# AXIS: THE ABSENCE OF LET-UP. The pressure does not come off — not when it is answered,
#   not when it is late, not when the other side has had enough — and none of it shows on
#   you. Black gives nothing away, so the reader's face is the same throughout; spicy means
#   it demands attention now; fried commits in the same motion as deciding.
# NOT: driven (spicy-fried-cannellini, batch 13 — SAME FLAVOUR AND SAME FORM, the sharpest
#   trap in the batch). DRIVEN IS MOTION TOWARD A GOAL WITH EVERYTHING ELSE EDITED AWAY:
#   the judo trial, the surveying diploma, the milk round at five, the promotion turned
#   down to keep the evenings. Every one of those five is a thing the reader WANTS, and the
#   cost is what they gave up for it. RELENTLESS HAS NO DESTINATION. The point is that it
#   does not stop, and the excess — remorseless — is failing to stop when a person in front
#   of you needs you to. TEST: if a facet would work equally for driven, it is driven and
#   it is wrong. So no ambitions, no training, no qualification, no career anywhere in this
#   entry, and nothing the reader is pursuing because they want the prize at the end.
#   NOT dogged (spicy-boiled-kidney, queued — endurance, taking it), NOT tireless
#   (spicy-boiled-mung, queued — capacity to keep going), NOT urgent (spicy-fried-mung,
#   queued — speed). Relentless is about the OTHER side never getting a break.
# DESIGN RULE: nothing shows on the reader's face and no facet may state that the reader
#   is angry, wound up, or enjoying it. The pole is legible from the count — the ninth,
#   the second morning, the third time this week — never from temperature.
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  remorseless — somebody in front of you has asked you to stop and has a plain
#         reason, and the pressure goes on, and what it does to them cannot be taken back.
#   HIGH  relentless — every marker says this is the point where people stop, and it costs
#         you something named, and you go again.
#   MID   relentless, low pitch — a small thing everyone else has written off, and you
#         keep at it past where anyone is watching, at a cost only to you.
#   LOW   relenting, low pitch — you take the pressure off once, deliberately, for a stated
#         reason, with what you are giving up named.
#   LEAST relenting — you let the whole thing go and are settled about it, with the price
#         of letting go visible on the page.
# === sweet-boiled-kidney — compassionate / pitying / hard-hearted
# AXIS: somebody is suffering, in front of you, and you go into it with them at a cost you
#   actually pay. Kidney puts itself between people it loves and harm; boiled is the steady
#   one others come to in order to be restored, which is why the reader can stay in the
#   room; sweet means it is for them and not for the reader's own account of themselves.
# NOT: kind (sweet-boiled-cannellini, batch 07 — SAME FLAVOUR AND SAME FORM). Kind is
#   GENEROSITY OF MANNER, given freely and cheaply — the rest of a library hour, saying the
#   man was out of order, taking the coffee. COMPASSIONATE REQUIRES SUFFERING ON THE PAGE
#   AND COSTS THE READER SOMETHING TO ANSWER. If nobody in the scene is in pain, or if the
#   answer is free, it is kind and it is wrong.
#   NOT sympathetic (sweet-fermented-kidney, queued — SAME BEAN, feeling with), NOT
#   nurturing (sweet-boiled-mung, queued — SAME FLAVOUR AND FORM, tending over time), NOT
#   solicitous (sour-roasted-mung, queued — attentiveness). The distinguishing feature here
#   is THE COST PAID TO GO IN, and that it is a single encounter rather than a regime.
# NOTE ON THE EXCESS: pitying is NOT giving too much. IT IS MAKING THE PERSON AN OBJECT —
#   their situation handled over their head, their standing taken from them by the manner
#   of the help. That has to be visible in the act itself, not asserted.
# POLES, as bare dispositions:
#   MOST  pitying — you take the person's trouble over and deal with it above them, in
#         front of others, and what they lose is their standing, and it cannot be undone.
#   HIGH  compassionate — real suffering, and you give up something concrete and named to
#         stay in it with them, on their level.
#   MID   compassionate, low pitch — a smaller trouble, a smaller cost, and you stay in it
#         where moving on was the ordinary thing to do.
#   LOW   hard-hearted, low pitch — you decline once to go in, and the reason is stated.
#   LEAST hard-hearted — the suffering is plainly in front of you and you leave it where it
#         is, openly, and are not troubled. A position, with its price on the page.
# ============ STEP 2 — what is off-limits ============
# fava: fortunes own the mustang that is caught and never ridden, "refuse it outright",
#   "saying no once saves saying it ten times", "do as asked this once", "going along costs
#   less than it looks", lamb fat and mint. OLD FACETS: a letter telling you to stop and
#   the same thing done again in daylight; an instruction refused in writing with two
#   people copied in; a rule questioned until somebody answers; work done exactly as asked
#   after one quiet objection; a brief changed again and redone over the weekend with
#   thanks. QUESTION owns missing float money and a manager who says the matter is closed.
#   FOUR OF THE FIVE OLD FACETS ARE AN OFFICE — a letter, an instruction, a rule, a brief.
#   That whole world is spent, and FACETS.md bans it anyway. No written objections, no
#   copying anybody in, no briefs, no managers.
# adzuki: fortunes own the sacred ibises mummified by the million, "take your hat off for
#   it", "ticket stubs outlive the trips", "it's only a thing", "use the good plates for
#   beans on toast", dried scallop and old soy. OLD FACETS: ninety seconds of totality with
#   every phone up; a bog body in a museum store and a hat coming off; a cathedral sat
#   through for the service; a telescope looked through once before the last bus; ashes
#   into the water and the first joke afterwards. QUESTION owns the oldest thing you own.
#   So NO eclipse, NO bog body, NO cathedral, NO telescope, NO ashes. Note the question is
#   entirely about an OLD OBJECT, which is antiquarian's territory — another reason nothing
#   in these five turns on a thing being old.
# mung: fortunes own the cleaner wrasse working inside the mouth of a bigger fish, "reveal
#   enough and people learn to guard what they say", "bringing it into the open helps",
#   "cover for them this once", "some things stay better hidden", kokum and rice husk. OLD
#   FACETS: four hours in the car and her father and the money; a life-drawing class and
#   the man who never speaks; a true thing said at a table and the next true thing said
#   after it; a grandfather asked about and the potatoes passed; a reunion and "people
#   drifted". QUESTION owns four in a kitchen and the quiet one on his father's drinking.
#   The old set is almost all SOMEBODY TALKING AT LENGTH while the reader listens, which is
#   confiding's shape, not this one. So no long confessions, no car journeys, no reunions.
#   What gets revealed here is mostly NOT SPEECH — a thing put where it can be seen.
# black: fortunes own the mako that has to keep swimming to breathe, "nothing finished ever
#   counts for long", "one more pass usually improves it", "an easy win still counts", "let
#   somebody else finish it", chipotle and unbroken heat. OLD FACETS: eight letters to the
#   water company and then the apology; a lodger dodging about the deposit, met outside his
#   work twice; ringing again about the drainage; a six-month claim dropped; one no from a
#   committee and the idea back in the drawer. QUESTION owns a maths set asked for twice.
#   So NO complaint letters, NO utilities, NO claims, NO chasing money, NO committees, NO
#   school requests. That burns the obvious half of this trait's territory, which is the
#   point: what is left is pressure ON A PERSON and going back out when everyone has gone in.
# kidney: fortunes own the elephant standing over a fallen one for hours, "pity somebody
#   enough and they become somebody to be pitied", "kindness costs less than it looks",
#   "treat them as capable", "hard-heartedness gets the difficult job done", coconut milk
#   and palm sugar. OLD FACETS: a man outside a bakery asked about the hostel and his
#   sister with a queue round you; a colleague's marriage taken out to the yard; a
#   neighbour at the gate about her boy; a friend let go for the third telling; a lost child
#   at the coconut shy left for the tea tent. QUESTION owns a towpath, twenty minutes, and a
#   husband gone into a home. So NO street begging, NO lost children, NO neighbour at a
#   gate, NO redundancy told repeatedly.
umami-roasted-fava

# ============ COLD READ (on the final text, after all editing) ============
# Fixed at the lint: one first-mention definite noun carrying a setting ("the trial"),
# one stack of clauses before the main verb, one facet over the same-shape cap in each
# of three entries, and three verbless flags that were the rule's fault, not the prose's
# — "stay", "delete" and "fell" were missing from the verb list in lint-facets.mjs and
# have been added. What remains in the linter is the per-entry median-length warning on
# all five (49-55 words), which fires on approved entries too.
# THE READ FOUND TWELVE, ELEVEN OF THEM IN THE CLOSING ACT and every one of them a noun
# the setup had never bought — half time with no match on the page, "yours" with no bag,
# a corridor, a bag on a concourse, a communion jug, a counter, a torch, a second machine
# with no first, a receptionist, a car, a brother of hers, and a dinner. Two more were
# POLE faults caught by the third list, not by the first two:
#   mung high — the letters were never said to contain anything, so putting them out read
#               as breaking a promise for its own sake rather than for her good. Now
#               "three appointments missed".
#   mung mid  — nothing on the page cost the reader anything, so asking the tutor to read
#               aloud was free and the low-pitch trait had no price. Now "two pages on
#               glazes that everybody else has started on".
# All are RE-READ below on the new text and marked.
# umami-roasted-fava
#  most  RE-READ. "at half time" needed a match, and the page had only put you outside a
#        club. Now "and you are both in the ground".
#        ON THE PAGE: you went over the hoardings when the club sold the training ground;
#        the ban says one more and the season ticket goes; the sale fell through a month
#        ago; the ticket is your dad's name as well as yours; thirty years of it; you are
#        both in the ground. ACT NEEDS: over = the hoardings; half time = the match you
#        are both at.
#        POLE NEEDS: insubordinate rather than defiant, and the clause that makes it is
#        "the sale fell through a month ago" — the cause is settled and you go anyway.
#        The sanction is real and stated, and it lands on somebody who is not you (thirty
#        years, his name). Cut either clause and this is ordinary defiance.
#        RESIST: stay in your seat.
#  high  ON THE PAGE: you reported the missing edge protection on the third floor; the
#        site manager has taken your shifts off you for it; he told the gang why; another
#        turn-up and it is for good. ACT NEEDS: the signing-in; seven; the work.
#        POLE NEEDS: defiant — a power that can actually do something, with the sanction
#        named twice (shifts gone, then for good), and the act done in the open under your
#        own name, which is the roasted part. This is not headstrong- nobody here is
#        merely of the opinion that you are wrong. RESIST: stay off.
#  mid   RE-READ. "You put yours back on your shoulder" had no bag of yours on the page.
#        Now "you have one from the shop up the road".
#        ON THE PAGE: the security man at the door; bags from other shops go behind his
#        desk; he can have you out if they do not; you have one from the shop up the road.
#        ACT NEEDS: it = your bag; your shoulder; in.
#        POLE NEEDS: defiant at low pitch — a standing instruction from somebody who can
#        eject you, visibly not complied with, and the whole cost is yours.
#        RESIST: hand it over.
#  low   ON THE PAGE: second day of a trial you have been called up for; the notebooks are
#        numbered and collected in every night; the witness said the man had done this
#        before; the judge has told the twelve of you to strike that or the trial starts
#        again; it is the only thing you have heard that explains anything.
#        ACT NEEDS: your note; the line.
#        POLE NEEDS: submissive at LOW pitch, and it must be an instruction obeyed rather
#        than agreeableness — the judge orders it, and the reason is stated (the trial
#        starts again). "The only thing you have heard that explains anything" is the
#        clause that makes obeying cost something; without it there is no vote.
#        RESIST: keep it in.
#  least ON THE PAGE: you are marshalling the road closure on a half marathon; control has
#        said on the radio that nobody crosses until the sweeper van is through; another
#        forty minutes; a woman with a pushchair; her mum's christening at eleven, four
#        streets away. ACT NEEDS: her; the van.
#        POLE NEEDS: the inverse fully — the instruction is taken as an instruction and
#        that is settled, not sour. Freedom (it is not yours to decide) and price (the
#        christening, which is what stops this being a facet about a rule nobody minds).
#        RESIST: let her over.
# umami-dried-adzuki
#  THE POINTING-UP CHECK, run on all five: in every one there is something on the page
#  larger than the reader — a birth, the painting, the two minutes, the church, the
#  funeral. None of them turns on a thing being old, which is the antiquarian guard.
#  most  RE-READ. "You go and stand out in the corridor" had no corridor. The midwife now
#        opens the door onto it.
#        ON THE PAGE: your friend asked you months ago to be the one in the room with her;
#        there is nobody else; her mum is four hours off; eleven hours in; the midwife
#        opens the door onto the corridor and says come on then.
#        ACT NEEDS: out there = the corridor.
#        POLE NEEDS: awestruck — the door is open, the invitation is spoken, and there is
#        no substitute for you ("nobody else", "four hours off"), so what stops you is the
#        size of it and nothing practical. That is the excess of reverence rather than
#        squeamishness, and it happens once. RESIST: go in.
#  high  ON THE PAGE: the one painting is in a room on its own; the ticket gives you ten
#        minutes in there; the three you came with did two minutes and are out in the
#        shop; their lift home goes now; the train instead is forty pounds.
#        ACT NEEDS: the room; the whole ten.
#        POLE NEEDS: reverential — the shortcut is on the page and has been taken by
#        everybody else, nobody would know, and the cost is priced (the lift, forty
#        pounds). RESIST: go with them.
#  mid   RE-READ. "You put your bag down" had no bag. The act is now "You stop where you
#        are for the whole two minutes", which uses only what the line states.
#        ON THE PAGE: eleven o'clock on the concourse; the tannoy asks for two minutes;
#        half the station keeps walking; your train goes from platform four in ninety
#        seconds. ACT NEEDS: where you are; the two minutes.
#        POLE NEEDS: reverential at low pitch — the observance is asked for, half the
#        people present decline it, and the ninety seconds is what it costs you and only
#        you. RESIST: get the train.
#  low   RE-READ. "the communion jug" and "the tap" both arrived at the act. The vestry
#        cupboard now has the jug in it and the little sink has the one tap.
#        ON THE PAGE: your friend cleans the church; she has taken you through the vestry;
#        the safe the registers live in; the little sink with the one tap; the cupboard
#        with the communion jug and the plate in it; the flowers for the morning need
#        water; nothing in there holds more than a cup. ACT NEEDS: the jug; the tap.
#        POLE NEEDS: profane at LOW pitch — the sacred object is put to plain use once and
#        the practical reason is stated and specific (nothing else holds more than a cup),
#        which is what holds it short of the inverse. RESIST: fill the cup ten times.
#  least RE-READ TWICE. "You put it on the counter" needed a counter, and the replacement
#        "get on with the dinner" needed a dinner. Now "You set it going and start
#        cooking", which needs nothing the line has not given.
#        ON THE PAGE: your great-aunt's funeral is being streamed; half the family are
#        abroad; you could not get the day off; your mum has asked you to watch it
#        properly. ACT NEEDS: it = the stream.
#        POLE NEEDS: the inverse fully — the rite is handled as ordinary material with the
#        ask stated in the same breath, which is what makes it a position rather than a
#        lapse. Freedom (it is only a screen) and price (your mum asked).
#        RESIST: sit down to it.
# sour-smoked-mung
#  THE KEPT-BACK CHECK, run on all five: every facet states why the thing was being held
#  out of sight — his dad's eight thousand, being put out of the house, nobody else there
#  knowing, eleven months in the kennel, parents who know nothing about the account.
#  Without the reason nothing is being uncovered and Accept collapses into "yes, I talk
#  about things".
#  most  ON THE PAGE: your friend's shop shut three weeks ago; he has not told his family;
#        his dad put the eight thousand in to start it; it is his dad's sixtieth; eleven
#        of you at the table; his sister asks how the shop is doing.
#        ACT NEEDS: them = the eleven at the table; what happened = the shop shutting.
#        POLE NEEDS: exposing rather than revealing — he did not choose the moment, the
#        room is the worst possible one, and the eleven cannot un-hear it. It serves the
#        answer to the question and not him. RESIST: let him answer.
#  high  RE-READ, AND THIS WAS A POLE FAULT. The letters were never said to contain
#        anything, so putting them out read as breaking a promise for its own sake. Now
#        "three appointments missed", which is what makes the revealing for her good.
#        ON THE PAGE: since the fall your mum tells everyone she is managing; the hospital
#        letters stay in the drawer; three appointments missed; if your brother sees them
#        he will have her out of the house; she made you promise; he is over on Sunday.
#        ACT NEEDS: the letters; him = your brother.
#        POLE NEEDS: revealing — the person who needs to see it sees it, it is for her
